commit.message:
DisableOverscroll instead of DisableBounce

Corrected the comment to use correct variable name, DisableOverscroll

test(v3,windows): keep the WebView2 lifetime tests valid under checkptr

go test -race enables checkptr, which aborts the process when a uintptr
is converted back into a pointer into the Go heap or stack without a
pointer in the same expression to derive it from. The edge tests that
stand in for native code made that conversion: they held a handler as a
bare address, as WebView2 does, and turned it back into a pointer to
read its vtable or look up its reference count. The QueryInterface stubs
did the same with their out-parameter. Under -race the package dies with
"checkptr: pointer arithmetic result points to invalid allocation" in
TestLiveDelayedControllerCallbackAfterAbandon.

A native reference is now a comRef: the address as an integer, which
still does not keep the handler alive, and the vtable read from the
handler while it was reachable. AddRef and Release call through that
vtable, reference counts are matched by address, and the abandoned
controller test captures the handler's Invoke slot before dropping it.
The QueryInterface stubs take the out-parameter as a typed pointer,
as the handlers' own callbacks take this.

What the tests verify is unchanged, and no production code changes.

fix(v3/linux): refresh systray menus on Menu.Update

On Linux a tray shows a dbusmenu layout that linuxSystemTray.setMenu
builds from the Menu. linuxMenu.update() only rebuilt the native menu, so
after tray.SetMenu(menu) a later menu.Clear(); menu.Add(...);
menu.Update() left the tray on the first menu forever. Windows already
rebuilds every tray popup built from the menu in update(); do the same on
Linux by rebuilding the layout of every tray whose menu is the updated
one, under the tray's itemMapLock as setMenu does.

The tray rebuild binds item.impl to the tray, so the gtk3 destroy hook no
longer saw itself as the owner and kept the activation handler entries of
items removed from a tray menu. Release them unless a newer native item
has taken the entry over.

commit.message:
test(v3,windows): keep the lifetime tests' host window out of allocation batches

The WebView2 lifetime tests prove that an abandoned Chromium no longer
retains its window by waiting for a weak pointer to the window to become
nil. Go does not promise that for a tiny pointer-free object: the tiny
allocator batches such objects into one allocation slot, and a weak
pointer into a batch stays non-nil while any object in it is referenced.

hostWindow was a single int, so without -race (which disables the tiny
allocator) it could share a slot with an allocation the replacement
Chromium keeps alive. TestLiveReplacementReleasesAbandonedHandlers then
failed intermittently with "abandoned Chromium retained its window".

hostWindow carries a pointer field, which keeps it out of any batch.
TestHostWindowIsCollectedBesideLiveObjects allocates windows beside live
pointer-free neighbours and requires each to be collected; it fails on
every run without the field.

No production code changes.

docs: add an H.264 source for the v3 release film so it plays on iPad Safari

The release film was AV1-only. Safari plays AV1 only on devices with a hardware
decoder (A17 Pro / M3 and newer), so older iPads showed a player that never
played. Add an H.264 High/AAC MP4 (21 MB, under the 25 MiB Cloudflare Pages
limit) as a second source in every locale. It was generated by M-Press v1.0.28,
which now warns about videos without an H.264 source and converts them.
